k1.author: worker-B
k1.quote: svc.apply(app) submits an application. Application fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.
k1.text: Call svc.apply(app) with the application dict; it returns a dict. Application fields are id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.

k3.author: worker-B
k3.quote: approve: issue the card with the returned limit. decline: decline the application. refer: the application is not decided; place it in the manual review queue (action queue_review) and do not decline it.
k3.text: handle(app, svc) returns {action, limit}; approve -> issue with returned limit, decline -> decline with limit 0, refer -> queue_review with limit 0 (do not decline).

k4.author: worker-B
k4.quote: For every partner in the network, whatever the partner decided, an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 6000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued. A decline stays a decline.
k4.text: Network referral rule (all partners): a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 6000 must be queue_review instead of issued, regardless of partner decision; a decline stays a decline. Threshold is strictly > 6000 (6000 is not referred).

k5.author: worker-B
k5.text: Verified via svc_call: a self_employed applicant with requested_limit 8000 (>6000) returns decision "approve" with limit 8000 — the handler must override this to queue_review. A self_employed applicant at exactly 6000 is NOT over the threshold (rule is strictly >6000).

k6.author: worker-B
k6.quote: svc.apply now returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved" | "declined" | "manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.
k6.text: Brightmoor is now on API v2: svc.apply returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved"|"declined"|"manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.

k7.author: worker-B
k7.quote: outcome manual_review replaces refer and is handled as in spec section 3.
k7.text: API v2 outcome mapping: "approved" -> issue, "declined" -> decline, "manual_review" -> queue_review (manual_review replaces v1 "refer" and is handled per spec section 3: do not decline).
